subject: Egress origination accounting & traffic classification for private connectors
messages:
From: Priya Rao <ops@keystone.com>
To: camila_reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Egress origin mapping + traffic classification request for private connectors

Hi Camila / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're starting the networking sign-off for the pilot and need to confirm a couple of things around how Redwood's private connectors will appear from our perimeter for allowlisting, logging, and traffic classification. A few concrete asks from our security and network teams: 

- Can Redwood provide a per-tenant / per-connection origination identifier (header or SNI) that we can use for downstream accounting?
- Do you require a stable set of egress IPs, or do you support short-lived/ephemeral NAT addresses (we run egress through a NAT gateway and prefer to minimize static ranges)?
- Which ports / FQDNs should be permitted for the control plane versus runtime model egress?
- Do you support mTLS and client certificate pinning for the control plane?

I've attached a rough diagram (keystone-egress-diagram-v1.pdf) showing our NAT topology and where we'd expect your private connector to sit.

If possible, we'd like to resolve this this week; otherwise please propose a 30-minute slot with ops and security.

Thanks,

Priya Rao
Sr. Cloud Engineer, Keystone Systems
ops@keystone.com

From: camila_reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>

Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Egress origin mapping + traffic classification request for private connectors

Hi Priya — great to hear from you and thanks for the diagram. Short answers up front, then details and next steps: 

- Per-origin metadata: Yes, we can emit a tenant identifier in a request header for runtime calls (X-Redwood-Tenant) and also preserve a per-connection UUID in the TLS SNI for control-plane handshake tracing. We treat the header as optional (customers may strip) but the SNI UUID is embedded when using our private connector.
- Egress IPs: We support both patterns. For highest assurance you can consume our documented set of stable egress IP ranges; alternatively we offer an ephemeral NAT mode where the connector leverages your gateway and we provide an attestation certificate bundle for short-lived IPs.
- Ports/FQDNs: Control plane (management, model pulls, heartbeats) uses 443 to control.redwood-inference.internal and requires mTLS. Runtime (inference token streams) uses 443 to model-runtime.redwood-inference.internal plus websocket upgrade endpoints on same host. We'll send a concise FQDN/port matrix in the next email.
- mTLS: Supported for control plane and strongly recommended for private deployments. We support mutual TLS with cert provisioning via your KMS/HSM-backed CSR flow or via our temporary cert issuance for pilot phases.

A couple of additional notes that matter for classification and audit: 
- We publish per-request logs containing timestamp, tenant-id (if header present), connector-uuid, and egress-ip in our audit bundle. We can redact prompt text by default and include token counts and response latency metrics.
- If you need strict allowlisting, the stable egress IP list will be required; ephemeral mode relies on attestation and periodic evidence exchange (we push an attestation signed by our control plane every 24h).

Next steps I propose:
1) Keystone confirms whether you prefer stable ranges or ephemeral NAT mode (reply inline).
2) We provide a one-page FQDN/port matrix + example iptables rules for your NAT gateway.
3) If stable ranges, we raise a short RFC and provide IP ranges and a timeline for cutover.

Are you available for a 30-min sync tomorrow (Fri) 10:30–11:00 PT? If not, we'll schedule early next week.

Best,

Camila — quick follow up from our security team after reading your note: we want to run pilot in ephemeral NAT mode first (to avoid expanding our existing perimeter). A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- Attestation cadence: 24h is fine, but we need a signed artifact we can ingest into our SIEM (JSON with connector-uuid, egress-ip(s), timestamp, signature). Can Redwood produce that format?
- SNI/headers: The team prefers SNI-based origination signals over headers when possible (less chance of intermediate stripping). Can you confirm the SNI approach will not leak tenant metadata to upstream third parties?

We're attaching a short appendix with our current NAT mapping (keystone-egress-appendix.xlsx). We'll be on the call Monday to align.

Thanks — Ben

Looping you both in to confirm internal owners and the operational plan for the Keystone pilot. Summary and action items below (please treat as our internal runbook update):

Summary: Keystone will run ephemeral NAT mode for pilot. They require: 1) signed 24h attestation JSON we push to their SIEM; 2) SNI-based origin signal (connector UUID) for control-plane TLS; 3) a one-page FQDN/port matrix and sample NAT/iptables rules.

Action items (owners):
- Camila: Draft the attestation JSON schema and example payload; add to Drive folder and circulate to Keystone (due Tue 2027-06-15). (attachment: redwood-egress-runbook-diff.patch)
- Laura: Produce the FQDN/port matrix and a minimal iptables snippet for NAT gateways (due Mon 2027-06-14).
- Michael: Verify our audit bundle includes connector-uuid and tenant-id fields and add redaction notes for PII (due Mon 2027-06-14).

Implementation notes for the runbook update:
- Attestation payload fields: connector_uuid, egress_ips (list), issued_at (ISO8601), signature_alg (edsig), signature (base64). We'll publish an HMAC + RSA signing option.
- SNI privacy: SNI will contain a randomly generated UUID per-connector (no tenant PII). We will document the entropy source and retention window; this provides downstream classification without exposing tenant names.
- Ephemeral mode: We'll include a 24h TTL for the certificate bundle and a replay-protected attestation counter.

I've filed INF-9821 to track the work and dropped the draft diff in the shared Drive link above. Priya/Ben — thanks for the appendix; we'll review and bring finalized artifacts to the Monday call.

Camila
